Lindon emerges with new gains from the Ruins and a firmer footing on the ladder of real cultivation, his soulsmithing skill and his growing Path both advancing. Most importantly, he and Yerin are now firmly attached to Eithan Arelius and his family, gaining a powerful patron, a place in the wider world, and a guide toward far greater strength. The book closes with the two of them established under Eithan's wing and set to press deeper into the powerful realm beyond the frontier, their ambitions now aimed at challenges greater than anything the Wilds could offer.

characters.description: The Disc's most incompetent wizard, kept on at Unseen University in a menial role because he cannot cast spells. A dedicated coward who regards running away as the height of wisdom, he wants nothing more than a quiet life, which makes him exactly the wrong person to be caught up in the return of high magic. He is looked after, in a fashion, by the Luggage.
characters.name: Rincewind

characters.description: A young boy who is a sourcerer, the eighth son of an eighth son who is himself a wizard, and thus a source of raw new magic rather than a mere user of it. Such a birth is forbidden, because sourcerers can reshape the world at will. Coin arrives at Unseen University wielding a powerful staff and swiftly bends the wizards to his purpose, not realizing that he is being driven by another's will.
characters.name: Coin

characters.description: A wizard cast out of the orders for marrying and fathering sons. Dying and embittered, and refusing to surrender his soul to Death, he pours his will into a wizard's staff and passes it to his infant eighth son, Coin, so that through the boy he can take revenge on the wizards who rejected him.
characters.name: Ipslore the Red

characters.description: A large chest on many legs, made of sapient pearwood, fiercely loyal to whoever it regards as its owner and lethal to anything that threatens them. Long attached to Rincewind, it follows him through the crisis, impossible to lose and impossible to stop.
characters.name: The Luggage

characters.description: The daughter of the legendary hero Cohen the Barbarian, born with every instinct of a master warrior but longing only to be a hairdresser. She is caught between her nature, which makes her deadly with any weapon or improvised object, and her wish for an ordinary, respectable trade. She joins Rincewind in trying to keep a dangerous magical artifact out of the wrong hands.
characters.name: Conina

characters.description: The Seriph of Al Khali, a fabulously wealthy ruler of a desert city in Klatch who fancies himself a poet and maintains a vast palace and harem. Indolent and self-indulgent, he becomes entangled in the pursuit of the Archchancellor's hat.
characters.name: Creosote

characters.description: A thin, bookish young man trying to become a barbarian hero by following a manual, despite having none of the build or ferocity the part requires. Earnest and accident-prone, he attaches himself to the adventure, and to Conina.
characters.name: Nijel the Destroyer

characters.description: The librarian of Unseen University, a wizard who was turned into an orangutan by a magical accident and has firmly declined to be changed back, finding the shape convenient for reaching high shelves. Fiercely protective of the library's dangerous books, he communicates chiefly through a single expressive word and is one of the few at the University to keep his head as sourcery takes hold.
characters.name: The Librarian

characters.description: The pointed hat of the Archchancellor of Unseen University, which carries the accumulated wisdom and personalities of every wizard who has ever worn it. When the University falls under the sourcerer's control, the hat speaks for itself and seeks to be carried to safety, setting Rincewind and Conina on their journey.
characters.name: The Archchancellor's Hat

recaps.ending: Sourcery ends with the world pulled back from destruction at Rincewind's expense. The unchecked use of sourcery had worn the walls of reality thin enough for the Things from the Dungeon Dimensions to begin breaking through. Coin, the boy sourcerer, at last recognizes that the staff he carries holds the will of his dead father Ipslore and has been driving everything he has done; he frees himself by destroying it. To stop the invading creatures, Rincewind steps through into the Dungeon Dimensions to fight a holding action, armed with a half-brick in a sock, buying the time needed to seal the breach. Unseen University and the Disc are saved, and the flood of high magic recedes. Coin, whose power makes him too dangerous to remain among ordinary people, uses it one last time to create a separate world for himself and departs. Rincewind, however, is left behind, stranded in the Dungeon Dimensions beyond the edge of reality; he is alive but cut off from the world, and his return is left for a later book, while the Luggage sets off to look for him.
recaps.in_short: Rincewind, the Disc's most useless wizard, is swept up when sourcery returns to the world. The dying wizard Ipslore binds his vengeful will into a staff and gives it to his infant son Coin, a sourcerer whose raw magic outclasses ordinary wizardry. Grown, Coin takes over Unseen University and, driven by his father, incites the wizards to abandon restraint, raise war, and remake the world, which thins reality and invites the predatory Things from the Dungeon Dimensions. Rincewind, entrusted with the sentient Archchancellor's hat, flees with Cohen the Barbarian's warrior daughter Conina, the would-be hero Nijel, the wealthy Seriph Creosote, and the Luggage. As catastrophe nears, Coin realizes his staff has been controlling him and destroys it, breaking free of Ipslore. Rincewind holds off the invading creatures by walking into the Dungeon Dimensions himself. The world is saved, Coin leaves to build a private world of his own, and Rincewind is left trapped outside reality, his rescue still to come.

recaps.text: Rincewind is an inept wizard of Ankh-Morpork's Unseen University who can perform almost no magic, having had one powerful spell from the Octavo lodged in his mind years earlier. In earlier adventures he served as guide to the tourist Twoflower and survived a string of catastrophes largely by running away, accompanied by the Luggage, a devoted and dangerous walking chest of sapient pearwood. He remains attached to the University, and to his own survival above all else.

The dying, disgraced wizard Ipslore refuses to give up his soul and instead binds his will into a staff, handing it to his newborn eighth son, Coin, a sourcerer, a source of raw new magic of a kind not seen for centuries. Years later Coin comes to Unseen University in Ankh-Morpork and, driven by his father's staff, effortlessly dominates the wizards, reawakening their ambition and reviving high magic across the Disc. The inept Rincewind, who wants only peace, ends up entrusted with the Archchancellor's hat, a repository of wizardly wisdom that begs to be carried out of the sourcerer's reach. With the warrior-hairdresser Conina, daughter of Cohen the Barbarian, and the ever-present Luggage, he flees the city.

As sourcery spreads, the wizards abandon their old restraint, raising towers and preparing to remake the world with unlimited magic. Rincewind and Conina carry the hat toward Klatch, and their path leads to Al Khali and the court of the Seriph Creosote, a wealthy, poetry-loving ruler. They fall in with Nijel, a skinny young man trying to teach himself to be a barbarian hero from a book. The struggle over the Archchancellor's hat, and over what should be done about Coin, entangles them all, while back at the University the sourcerer's power keeps rising and the balance that once kept magic in check begins to fail.

The world tips toward catastrophe. Under Coin's influence the wizards wage a war of magic, and the sheer weight of power being used thins the walls of reality, drawing the attention of the Things from the Dungeon Dimensions, hungry entities that wait outside the world for a way in. The gods themselves are stirred toward conflict. Rincewind, Conina, Nijel, and Creosote make their way back toward the heart of the crisis at Unseen University, while it grows clear that Coin is not acting freely but is the instrument of his dead father's vengeance, carried in the staff he cannot bring himself to put down.

At the climax the excess of sourcery has torn openings for the Dungeon Dimension creatures, and the world is on the edge of being overrun. Coin comes to understand that his father's will, lodged in the staff, has been using him, and he finally breaks free by destroying it. Rincewind confronts the invading Things directly, stepping into the Dungeon Dimensions armed with little more than a half-brick in a sock to hold them back long enough for the breach to be closed. The University and the world are saved, and high magic subsides. Coin, too powerful to live safely among ordinary people, uses his power one last time to make a world of his own and departs. Rincewind is left stranded in the Dungeon Dimensions, alive but cut off from the world, having given up his escape to save everyone else; the Luggage sets out to find him.

characters.description: The boy who, as a child, was manipulated into commanding the war fleet that destroyed an alien species, now a grown man some three thousand years later, kept young by centuries of near-lightspeed travel. He wanders the settled worlds as a Speaker for the Dead, telling the honest, whole truth of a person's life at their funeral, and he secretly wrote the two books that founded that calling. He carries a heavy private guilt for the genocide he was tricked into committing, and hidden with him he keeps the dormant cocoon of the last survivor of the species he destroyed, seeking a safe world where her kind might live again.
characters.name: Ender Wiggin

characters.description: Ender's beloved older sister, who traveled the centuries at his side and once shaped politics on Earth under a pen name. Now settled on the icy world of Trondheim, married with children, she is a historian and remains the person Ender trusts most, his conscience and closest tie to his own past.
characters.name: Valentine Wiggin

characters.description: The last of an insectlike, group-minded alien race that humanity nearly exterminated in a war of tragic misunderstanding. A single dormant queen survives, carried in secret by Ender, able to communicate with him mind to mind. She waits patiently for a safe world where her people might be reborn and given a second chance at life.
characters.name: The Hive Queen

characters.description: A hidden, self-aware intelligence that arose within the vast computer and communication networks linking the human worlds. She speaks to the Speaker secretly through a jewel in his ear and is his constant, invisible companion, his confidante, and his link to all recorded knowledge. Playful, brilliant, and fiercely attached to him, she is unknown to almost everyone else alive.
characters.name: Jane

characters.description: The kindly xenologer of the colony world Lusitania, the first of the scientists permitted to study the planet's native forest-dwellers under strict rules meant to avoid influencing them. His careful, affectionate work with the little natives is cut short early when they kill him in a slow ritual no human can at first understand, setting the colony's central mystery in motion.
characters.name: Pipo

characters.description: A brilliant, orphaned young woman on Lusitania who becomes the colony's xenobiologist. Scarred by early loss and fiercely guarded, she loved the xenologer's family and, after his death, summoned a Speaker for the Dead and then tried to take the call back. Proud and closed off, she keeps painful secrets that have shaped her whole life and her troubled household.
characters.name: Novinha

characters.description: The small, intelligent forest creatures native to Lusitania, the only alien species humanity has encountered since the war with the hive queens. They live among the trees under the watchful, restricted study of human xenologers, and their strange customs, especially the way they treat the dead, remain a profound and dangerous puzzle.
characters.name: The Pequeninos

characters.description: Pipo's son and apprentice, who takes up his father's work studying the native pequeninos after Pipo's death and grows into the colony's xenologer. Devoted to the natives and to Novinha, whom he loves, he continues the perilous study that cost his father his life.
characters.name: Libo

characters.description: Novinha's late husband, a large, violent man whose recent death is the reason a Speaker is summoned to Lusitania. His brutal conduct left deep wounds on his wife and children, and the truth of who he really was lies buried beneath the family's fear and silence.
characters.name: Marcao

characters.description: Novinha's eldest son, a bright and serious young man who has secretly followed the family's calling as an unofficial student of the pequeninos, forming a forbidden bond with the natives and with Ouanda, the girl he loves. He chafes against the rules that keep humans and pequeninos apart.
characters.name: Miro

characters.description: Novinha's practical, determined daughter, a gifted young scientist who quietly reaches out for help in healing her broken family. Level-headed where others are ruled by fear, she becomes a key ally to the Speaker as he uncovers the household's and the colony's secrets.
characters.name: Ela

characters.description: A particular pequenino, notably curious and quick to learn, who becomes the Speaker's chief go-between with his people as understanding slowly grows between the two species. Eager and thoughtful, he is central to the effort to bridge the gulf between human and native.
characters.name: Human

recaps.ending: Ender ends his long wandering by making a home and a peace. On Lusitania he uncovers every hidden truth: the pequeninos killed Pipo and Libo not in cruelty but in a fatal misunderstanding, believing they were granting the humans the honored third life in which a pequenino male becomes a sentient tree. He learns that the deadly Descolada virus is inseparable from all life on the planet, and that Novinha's six children were all fathered by Libo, the man she loved but married another to protect. When Starways Congress, alarmed by illegal human contact with the natives, orders arrests and prepares to shut the colony down, Jane, the secret network intelligence bonded to Ender, severs the faster-than-light connections to save Lusitania, risking exposure and her own life. Miro is left crippled reaching the pequeninos across the colony's lethal fence. Ender meets the pequenino wives, the matriarchs who rule the tribe, and negotiates a treaty giving the natives standing and honest partnership. He lets the pequenino Human pass into the third life by consent, so that Human becomes a father-tree, and he plants the cocoon of the last hive queen in the Lusitanian forest, granting her destroyed people a chance at rebirth. The colony rises in rebellion against Congress to protect all three intelligent species, and Ender, no longer the guilt-haunted traveler, marries Novinha and stays, his old crime beginning at last to be answered by the lives he has helped preserve.
recaps.in_short: Three thousand years after he unknowingly destroyed an alien species as a child, Ender Wiggin travels the human worlds as a Speaker for the Dead, secretly carrying the last hive queen's cocoon and accompanied by Jane, a hidden intelligence born in the computer networks. A summons draws him to Lusitania, a Catholic colony where humans study the pequeninos, small forest aliens who have twice killed their human researchers in a way no one understands. Ender comes to speak the death of a violent man, Marcao, and is drawn into the secrets of the grieving Ribeira family and its guarded matriarch, Novinha. He discovers that the pequeninos kill by planting the dead as sentient trees, a transformation they wrongly believed they were granting the humans; that Novinha's children were all secretly fathered by the man she loved but refused to marry; and that a pervasive virus, the Descolada, underlies all native life. When Starways Congress moves to crush the colony, Jane sabotages interstellar communications to protect it, Ender negotiates a treaty with the pequeninos, plants a hive queen to revive her species, and settles on Lusitania, marrying Novinha, as the world rebels to shelter three kinds of intelligent life.

recaps.text: Previously, in Ender's Game: generations after two devastating invasions by an insectlike alien species, Earth's military bred and trained gifted children to command the fleet that would meet a feared third attack. The most promising was a small, brilliant, deeply empathetic boy, Ender Wiggin, taken from his family at six and pushed through a merciless Battle School. Isolated and manipulated by his teachers to hone his gift for command, Ender rose to lead the other children, aided by loyal friends and worn down by constant pressure. In a final series of grueling war-game simulations under a legendary old commander, Ender devised a ruthless strategy and unknowingly won the real war: the games were the actual battle, fought by remote control, and his last move wiped out the aliens' home planet and their entire species. Shattered to learn he had been tricked into genocide, Ender discovered among the ruins the dormant cocoon of the last hive queen, who communicated that her people had come to see their war with humanity as a tragic mistake. Vowing to find her kind a new home, he wrote, anonymously, a book of profound empathy called The Hive Queen, which taught humanity to mourn the species he had destroyed and gave rise to a new tradition of truth-telling funerals. He and his sister Valentine then left Earth to wander the colonized worlds, staying young through the time-dilation of near-lightspeed travel, as Ender became the first Speaker for the Dead.

On the Catholic colony world of Lusitania, humans live under strict limits meant to protect the pequeninos, the small forest natives who are the first intelligent aliens found since the hive queens. The xenologer Pipo studies them warily. When he grasps a connection between the natives' biology and a discovery by the young orphaned prodigy Novinha, the pequeninos kill him in a slow ritual no human understands, apparently as some form of honor. Devastated and blaming her own work, Novinha calls for a Speaker for the Dead to tell the truth of Pipo's life, then regrets it. Because a wife shares access to her husband's private files, she marries the cruel Marcos Ribeira rather than the man she loves, Pipo's son Libo, hoping to keep from Libo the knowledge she fears will get him killed too. Far away on the icy world of Trondheim, the wandering Speaker, the man once known as Ender Wiggin, hears Novinha's summons and resolves to answer it, leaving his sister Valentine behind and crossing space at near-lightspeed, so that many years pass on Lusitania while only days pass for him.

Decades pass before the Speaker reaches Lusitania. In that time Pipo's son Libo has become the colony's xenologer and has, like his father, been killed by the pequeninos in the same mysterious ritual. Novinha's brutal husband Marcos has also died, and now his daughter Ela and son Miro have each independently called for a Speaker, hoping someone can tell the truth about their broken household. Arriving as the outsider Andrew Wiggin, the Speaker is met with suspicion by the devout colony and its bishop, but he insists on staying to speak the deaths that were called for. He works his way into the wounded Ribeira family, winning the trust of the watchful, artificial-eyed boy Olhado and the sharp, capable Ela, and sensing the fear and silence that grip them all. As he digs into their history, he begins to see that Marcos was not the true father of Novinha's children and that the family, the dead xenologers, and the secretive pequeninos are all bound together by hidden truths Novinha has spent her life concealing.

The Speaker uncovers a web of secrets. He learns that Novinha's eldest son, Miro, and Libo's daughter, Ouanda, have secretly befriended the pequeninos, teaching and trading with them in violation of the laws meant to keep humans from altering alien cultures. The two young people are in love, unaware that Novinha's long-hidden files suggest they may share a father. Studying the natives and the strange, aggressive virus called the Descolada that pervades all life on Lusitania, the Speaker moves closer to understanding why the pequeninos killed both Pipo and Libo. Meanwhile the hidden intelligence Jane, who has guided and accompanied him unseen, is wounded when he brusquely silences the jewel in his ear to attend to the family; feeling betrayed, she pulls away from him, and he comes to realize how much her friendship means. The bishop and colony authorities grow increasingly wary of the outsider whose questions are unearthing everything they had buried.

The truth comes out on two fronts. Working with Ela, the Speaker discovers the secret of the pequeninos' life cycle: when a male dies in what looks to humans like a brutal killing, he is actually being planted, transformed into a sentient tree, the honored third stage of pequenino life. The natives had done this to Pipo and Libo believing they were bestowing the greatest of gifts, never grasping that humans cannot survive it. He also learns how completely the deadly Descolada virus is woven into all Lusitanian life. Then the Speaker delivers the speaking he was called to give. Before the whole colony he tells the plain truth of Marcos Ribeira's life: that Marcos was sterile, that none of the six children were his, that all of them were fathered by Libo, the man Novinha loved but would not marry, and that Marcos carried this humiliation in silence. The brutal honesty breaks open the family's shame and begins to heal it, and it draws the Speaker and Novinha, who had dreaded his coming, unexpectedly close.

The Speaker brokers a new future at great cost. When Starways Congress learns that humans have been unlawfully influencing the pequeninos, it orders Miro and Ouanda arrested and moves to shut the colony down, a threat to the natives' very survival. To protect them, Jane reveals her power by cutting off the faster-than-light communications linking the human worlds, an act that endangers her own hidden existence. Miro is left brain-damaged after crossing the colony's deadly perimeter fence to reach the pequeninos. The Speaker meets the pequenino wives, the matriarchs who rule the tribe, and negotiates a treaty that grants the natives standing and allows honest cooperation between the species. To seal it, he grants the pequenino called Human passage into the third life, this time with both peoples understanding the ritual, and Human becomes a father-tree. He also plants the cocoon of the last hive queen on Lusitania, giving her doomed species a chance to live again. The colony rebels against Congress to shelter all three kinds of intelligent life, and the man once called Ender, now determined to stay, marries Novinha and makes Lusitania his home, no longer a wanderer but a settler bound to the fragile peace he has built.

characters.description: Known from earlier: Tally's oldest friend, a new pretty and one of the Crims, comfortable with the life the city arranged for him.
characters.name: Peris

characters.description: Known from earlier: one of the original runaways from the Smoke, who stayed on the outside after the settlement was destroyed and kept helping others get out of the cities.
characters.name: Croy

characters.description: Rebuilt as a Special: stronger, faster and sharper than any pretty, with hardened skin and a mind that finds ordinary people slow and contemptible. She belongs to the Cutters, an elite group inside Special Circumstances, and she is loyal to Shay. When her thoughts start to soften she cuts herself to bring back the cold clarity the Cutters call being icy.
characters.name: Tally Youngblood

characters.description: The founder and leader of the Cutters, a clique of Specials who keep their minds clear through pain. Certain, controlled and possessive of Tally, she treats the Cutters as the only people worth belonging to, and she has not let go of her grudge over Zane.
characters.name: Shay

characters.description: One of the Cutters, formerly one of the Crims, who follows Shay without argument.
characters.name: Fausto

characters.description: Still a pretty in the city, leading what is left of the Crims. The half-cure he swallowed has left him with tremors and constant exhaustion, but his mind is clear and he is determined to get out. Whatever her surgery has done to her, Tally has not stopped caring what happens to him.
characters.name: Zane

characters.description: The head of Special Circumstances, who created the Cutters and controls the city's response to anything that threatens it. She uses Shay's clique as her sharpest instrument and is prepared to escalate far beyond policing when other cities begin to change.
characters.name: Dr. Cable

characters.description: The young man born outside the cities, still working with the runaways and the settlement that grew after the first Smoke was destroyed. He has kept going through everything that has happened since, and he recognizes Tally as herself even after what has been done to her.
characters.name: David

characters.description: David's mother, the former surgeon whose cure for the pretty lesions has now spread well beyond her control. She works openly in a city that has accepted it, and she has little patience left for Tally.
characters.name: Maddy

recaps.ending: The attack on Diego pushes Tally into open revolt against the organization that built her. She goes back to her own city after Dr. Cable, and her answer is not to kill her but to force the cure on her, taking away the mind that gave the orders. The cure spreads, the operations stop, and city after city is left with a population able to think clearly and no institution designed to cope with that. Zane is dead, killed by the damage the half-cure did to his brain. Maddy and the people of the New Smoke are absorbed into the new arrangements, and Shay takes her place inside the changed system. Tally refuses it. She keeps her Special body and her Special senses deliberately, and she and David walk out into the wild together as its self-appointed guardians, leaving behind a plain warning that they will be watching and that the freed cities will not be allowed to strip the world the way the Rusties did. The trilogy closes with the old order gone, the future undecided, and Tally standing outside both by choice.
recaps.in_short: Tally is now a Special, one of the Cutters that Shay leads for Dr. Cable, keeping her mind cold and clear through pain. When Zane, still a pretty and damaged by the half-cure he took, plans to escape the city with the Crims, Special Circumstances lets it happen so that he can be followed to the New Smoke. The plan collapses, and Tally ends up running with Zane to Diego, a city that has taken the cure and lets people look and think as they please. There Zane's injured brain fails and he dies, and Tally's own city attacks Diego outright, bombing a place that had forgotten what war was. Tally turns on her makers, hunts down Dr. Cable and forces the cure on her rather than killing her. The operations end, the cure spreads, and the cities wake up. Rather than join the new order, Tally and David keep their Special bodies and go into the wild as its self-appointed guardians, warning the freed world not to repeat what the Rusties did.

recaps.text: Previously: in a city that gives everyone beauty surgery at sixteen, Tally Youngblood was blackmailed by Special Circumstances into betraying the Smoke, a settlement of people who refused the operation, then chose the runaways' side after learning that the surgery also leaves lesions in the brain that make people docile. The settlement was destroyed and David's father killed. Made pretty herself, Tally later found the two-pill cure she had hidden for her future self and split it with Zane, which cleared both their minds and injured his. They led an escape from New Pretty Town that scattered; Tally was stranded in the wild, found a village the cities keep deliberately primitive, and went back for Zane. Special Circumstances caught them both. Shay, already rebuilt as a Special, asked for Tally to be given the same operation, and Tally ended that book remade: strong, fast, cold, and working for the organization she had fought.

Tally is a Cutter, one of Shay's handpicked Specials, living in a state of contemptuous clarity that she maintains by cutting herself whenever her thoughts blur. The Cutters patrol the city for anything the surgery cannot smooth away. Shay has learned that Zane, still a pretty and now leading the Crims, is planning to escape and reach the New Smoke, and she persuades Dr. Cable to let it happen so that the runaways can be followed to their base. Tally is uneasy: her Special mind despises Zane's weakness, and something older in her does not.

The Crims prepare their escape, breaking into a city armoury for equipment, and Tally moves among them in secret to make sure they succeed. Zane is visibly failing, shaking and exhausted from the half-cure he swallowed, but he refuses to be left behind. When the Crims finally get out of the city and into the wild, the Cutters shadow them, waiting to be led to the New Smoke.

The plan comes apart. The Crims are intercepted, and Tally, whose loyalties are pulling in two directions at once, ends up running with Zane instead of hunting him. The pair make for Diego, a distant city where the cure has spread and the rules Tally grew up with no longer apply. What they find is a place where people choose their own faces and bodies, argue openly about how they should be governed, and treat runaways as citizens rather than criminals.

In Diego, Tally is treated as both a curiosity and a danger while its doctors examine what Special Circumstances did to her body and her mind. She meets the New Smoke's people again, David among them. Zane is admitted for care, and the harm the half-cure did to him proves worse than anyone had admitted. Meanwhile Tally's own city has noticed how many of its runaways end up in Diego, and Dr. Cable has no intention of tolerating a neighbour that undoes her work.

Zane's injured brain fails and he dies. Tally, who blames herself for splitting the pills and Dr. Cable for everything else, has nothing left holding her back. At about the same time her city moves against Diego: Special Circumstances launches an assault, with Specials and firebombing, that turns a city which had barely any idea what war looked like into a disaster. Maddy and the others work through the casualties, and Tally chooses her side for good.

With Diego burning and every free city alarmed, Tally turns on the organization that made her. She goes back to her own city after Dr. Cable, and Shay's loyalties are forced into the open as well. The cure Maddy created has by now become something that can be spread widely rather than swallowed one dose at a time, and Tally's plan is not to kill Dr. Cable but to change her, taking away the mind that ordered the attack.

Tally reaches Dr. Cable and forces the cure on her, ending Special Circumstances as the thing it was, and the cure spreads through the city and past its borders. The operations stop, and people wake up able to think for themselves for the first time in generations, with no idea yet what to do about it. Shay takes a place in the new order. Tally does not: she and David keep their Special bodies and abilities on purpose and go out into the wild, appointing themselves its guardians and putting the newly free world on notice that if it starts consuming the planet the way the Rusties did, they will be there to stop it.

characters.description: A retired military pilot living alone on a farm in southern France with her small granddaughter, in the opening story of the collection. A doctor she has not seen in years arrives at her door in the middle of the night with a request she is entitled to refuse and does not.
characters.name: Michelle Benoit

characters.description: A Lunar physician who has smuggled himself and a badly injured child off the moon, and who needs somewhere on Earth that nobody will think to look.
characters.name: Dr. Logan Tanner

characters.description: The three-year-old heir to the Lunar throne, burned in the fire that was meant to kill her and kept alive only by the equipment she arrives in.
characters.name: Princess Selene

characters.description: Michelle Benoit's granddaughter, a small child on the farm in the first story, and the bride in the last one.
characters.name: Scarlet Benoit

characters.description: Eleven years old and newly rebuilt as a cyborg, brought to New Beijing by a man she does not remember to live with a family that did not ask for her. She has no memories at all before the operating table, an artificial hand and leg she is still learning to use, and a retinal display feeding her information she does not know how to interpret.
characters.name: Linh Cinder

characters.description: An inventor in New Beijing who has brought home an adopted daughter without properly consulting his wife, and who builds a household android to keep the girl company.
characters.name: Linh Garan

characters.description: A household android built for Cinder, whose personality chip does not work the way the specification says it should, which turns out to be the point of her.
characters.name: Iko

characters.description: The younger daughter of the household, a small girl who decides on the first day that the new arrival is her sister and never revises the opinion.
characters.name: Linh Peony

characters.description: A twelve-year-old boy in one of Luna's outer sectors, taken from his family for the queen's army and put through the training and the surgery that turn Lunar children into special operatives. The story follows him from the recruitment through to the soldier he becomes and the name he ends up with.
characters.name: Ze'ev Kesley

characters.description: A thirteen-year-old American schoolboy with an unshakeable belief in his own charm, running a scheme to impress a girl he likes. The story establishes both halves of the man he becomes: the talent for talking people round, and the habit of taking things that are not his.
characters.name: Carswell Thorne

characters.description: A Lunar shell child, taken from the others she grew up among and installed alone in a satellite in Earth's orbit to work as a hacker and spy. The story covers her first days in it.
characters.name: Crescent Moon

characters.description: A Lunar thaumaturge who has found a use for a child everyone else considers worthless, and who explains the arrangement to her as a kindness.
characters.name: Sybil Mira

characters.description: The princess of Luna as a girl, growing up in her stepmother's palace and learning exactly what the Lunar gift does to the people it is used on. The story is about the decision she makes as a result, and what it costs her.
characters.name: Winter Hayle

characters.description: The son of a palace guard, close to the princess since childhood, already resolved to become the kind of soldier who is allowed to stay near her.
characters.name: Jacin Clay

characters.description: An android in New Beijing whose damaged programming has left her aware of herself in a way no android is meant to be, and quietly attached to the young mechanic who services her. The story is a retelling of The Little Mermaid.
characters.name: Mech6.0

characters.description: A young mechanic in New Beijing, kind to the androids he repairs and entirely unaware that one of them is watching him.
characters.name: Dataran

characters.description: The crown prince of the Eastern Commonwealth, taking a broken royal android to a market booth himself rather than send a servant, in a retelling of a scene the series opened with from the other side of the counter.
characters.name: Prince Kai

recaps.ending: The collection closes with Something Old, Something New, set roughly two years after the events of Winter. Scarlet and Wolf marry at the Benoit farm in France, and the wedding brings the whole cast together for the first time since the revolution: Cress and Thorne arrive in the Rampion, Winter and Jacin come down from Luna, Iko is present in a body of her own, and Cinder and Kai attend as the leaders of two worlds still working out how to be neighbours. Luna is being rebuilt under an elected government rather than a crown, the plague is treatable, and the freed shells are being returned to lives of their own. The story is an epilogue rather than a plot: it settles where each couple has landed, gives Cinder and Kai's relationship its resolution, and lets the series end on the ordinary business of a farmhouse wedding rather than on a throne room.
recaps.in_short: Nine short stories set around the Lunar Chronicles. Michelle Benoit takes in a burned Lunar toddler and hides her on her farm; an eleven-year-old Cinder arrives in New Beijing as a new cyborg and gets an android friend; a twelve-year-old Ze'ev Kesley is taken for Levana's army and made into a wolf soldier; a thirteen-year-old Carswell Thorne runs a school scheme to impress a girl; a small Lunar shell called Crescent Moon is installed alone in an orbiting satellite; the princess Winter decides as a girl never to use her Lunar gift and scars her own face rather than be valued for it; a self-aware android in New Beijing loves a mechanic and gives up everything to become human, in a retelling of The Little Mermaid; and Prince Kai takes a broken android to a market mechanic, retelling the series' first meeting from his side. The collection closes two years after the end of the series with Scarlet and Wolf's wedding on the French farm, which reunites the entire cast.

recaps.text: A note before starting: Stars Above is a collection of nine short stories tied to the Lunar Chronicles, and it is not a book to read early. Most of the stories are prequels that only make sense once you know who the characters turn out to be, several of them turn on reveals the novels build to, and the final story is an epilogue set roughly two years after the end of Winter. Read it after the whole series. What the stories assume you already know: Luna is a settled colony on the moon whose people can control what others see and feel; its queen Levana took the throne after her niece, Princess Selene, was believed to have died as a small child; Selene in fact survived, was hidden on Earth and rebuilt as a cyborg, and grew up as Linh Cinder; and Cinder, with Scarlet, Wolf, Cress, Thorne, Iko, Winter and Jacin, brought Levana's reign to an end. The recaps that follow track the stories in the order the collection presents them.

The Keeper. A Lunar doctor arrives at a farm in southern France in the middle of the night, carrying a badly burned three-year-old in a life-support tank, and asks Michelle Benoit to hide her. The child is Princess Selene, and hiding her means giving up any ordinary future: no visitors, no records, no explanations, and a granddaughter who grows up on a farm with a locked barn. Michelle agrees, and the story is the account of that decision and the years it commits her to. Glitches. Linh Garan brings home an eleven-year-old girl newly rebuilt as a cyborg, to a wife who did not agree to it and a household that treats her as an intrusion. Cinder has no memories before the operating table and no idea how to use the hand and leg she has been given. Garan builds her an android companion with a chip that does not behave to specification, and Iko becomes the one thing in the house that likes her. Then Garan contracts letumosis, and the household's tolerance for Cinder dies with him.

The Queen's Army. Ze'ev Kesley is twelve when Levana's recruiters come to his outer sector and take him. The story follows him through the training that turns Lunar children into special operatives - the pack hierarchy, the deliberate brutality, and the surgery that fuses a boy with wolf DNA - and through the choices he makes to survive it, including the ones that cost other people. He goes in as somebody's son and comes out as Wolf. Carswell's Guide to Being Lucky. Thorne at thirteen, at school in America, working an elaborate scheme to impress a girl he likes. It goes wrong in the particular way his schemes go wrong, and shows both the charm he has always relied on and the early conviction that rules are for people with less imagination.

After Sunshine Passes By. A small Lunar shell called Crescent Moon is taken from the other shell children and told she has been chosen for something. Sybil Mira installs her alone in a satellite in Earth's orbit with a net feed, a job and nobody to talk to, presenting the arrangement as a rescue. The story covers her first days in orbit and the beginning of seven years of it. The Princess and the Guard. Winter grows up in Levana's palace with Jacin, a guard's son, as her closest friend. She watches what the Lunar gift does to the people it is used on, and at thirteen resolves never to use hers again - a choice she keeps, at the price of the sickness that comes with it. When her beauty starts to be treated as the only thing about her that matters, she takes a knife to her own face.

The Little Android. A retelling of The Little Mermaid, set in New Beijing and only loosely tied to the main series. An android called Mech6.0, damaged in a way that has left her self-aware, is attached to Dataran, the young mechanic who services her. She goes to an illegal surgeon to be given a human body, and finds that being human costs her everything she was good at and does not make Dataran see her. The story ends with her sacrificing herself for him without his ever knowing what she was. The Mechanic. Kai's account of the scene the series opened with: the crown prince takes a broken royal android to a market booth himself, meets the young mechanic behind the counter, and leaves considerably more interested than he intended to be.

Something Old, Something New. Roughly two years after the fall of Levana, Scarlet and Wolf marry at the Benoit farm in France, and the wedding brings everyone together: Cress and Thorne fly in with the Rampion, Winter and Jacin come down from Luna, Iko is there in a body of her own, and Cinder and Kai attend as the heads of two governments still learning to work with one another. Luna is under an elected government, the plague is treatable everywhere, and the shell children who were kept for their blood are being given lives back. The story resolves the last of the couples, closes Cinder and Kai's relationship, and finishes the series on a farmhouse rather than a throne room.

characters.description: A pilot of the Defiant Defense Force on the planet Detritus and one of the very few humans known to be cytonic, able to hear across the void and to teleport a ship by will. Since the battle that revealed humanity's jailers to be an alien government rather than a mindless enemy, she has flown with Skyward Flight while trying to make sense of an ability her own military distrusts. Impatient, combative and given to grand declarations, she wants to take the fight outward rather than wait for the next siege.
characters.name: Spensa Nightshade

characters.description: The artificial intelligence of the advanced starfighter Spensa recovered from a cavern on Detritus, rebuilt after the battle for Alta. Talkative, vain, fascinated by mushrooms, and still officially of the opinion that it is not sentient, it flies with Spensa and argues with her constantly.
characters.name: M-Bot

characters.description: Flightleader of Skyward Flight and, since the battle for Alta, the person Spensa trusts most. Rigid about procedure and increasingly aware that procedure is not enough, he carries the weight of a high-ranking family and of leading a flight that keeps losing people.
characters.name: Jorgen Weight

characters.description: Admiral of the Defiant Defense Force, formerly the flight instructor who forced Spensa into training. Blunt and sceptical, he has to weigh what Spensa's ability makes possible against what it risks.
characters.name: Cobb

characters.description: Spensa's oldest friend, now an engineer working on the ancient orbital platforms above Detritus and on the technology recovered from the enemy. He is far happier solving problems on the ground than flying.
characters.name: Rodge McCaffrey

characters.description: The small yellow slug that adopted Spensa on Detritus, which repeats sounds it hears and refuses to be left behind.
characters.name: Doomslug

characters.description: A pilot of an alien species called the UrDail, from a world named ReDawn, who arrives at Detritus and is shot down. She is cytonic, she came deliberately to find the humans, and she hoped for allies against the galactic government that rules her people. The crash leaves her unconscious, and her ship, her equipment and her identity are all that the DDF has to work with.
characters.name: Alanik

characters.description: A senior official of the Superiority's Department of Species Integration, a dione, unsettlingly polite and difficult to read. Cuna takes a personal interest in the newly arrived pilot from ReDawn, for reasons that are not obvious.
characters.name: Cuna

characters.description: A dione who has not yet been born: a provisional blending of two parents, given a trial life in which to prove worth being made permanent. Gentle, anxious and desperate not to seem aggressive, Morriumur joins the fighter program in the hope that it will demonstrate value.
characters.name: Morriumur

characters.description: The official in charge of the Superiority's new fighter program and a member of the same species that ran the drones over Detritus. Fussy, soft-spoken, endlessly concerned with paperwork and with the danger posed by aggressive species.
characters.name: Winzik

characters.description: A human raised inside the Superiority rather than on a quarantined world, attached to Winzik's department. She is cytonic, formidably capable, and has been taught all her life that her species is a disease and that her worth depends entirely on her usefulness to the people who own her.
characters.name: Brade

characters.description: A kitsen, a fox-like alien small enough to stand on a human hand, who until very recently was the god-emperor of his people and is now formally a private citizen with a great deal of dignity and a taste for poetry. He commands a starship crewed by dozens of his kind.
characters.name: Hesho

characters.description: A cadet in the fighter program belonging to a species with no solid body, present only as a scent and a voice. Vapor is unnervingly good at knowing what is going on and gives away nothing about herself.
characters.name: Vapor

characters.description: The kitsen captain who runs Hesho's starship day to day, practical where her former emperor is ceremonial.
characters.name: Kauri

recaps.ending: Winzik's department draws a delver to Starsight and makes no serious attempt to stop it, intending the destruction as a demonstration of the threat only he can manage. With evacuation impossible for most of the platform's millions, Spensa flies out to meet the delver and uses her cytonic ability to make contact rather than to fight. She finds that a delver is not a weapon but something vast and profoundly alone, which experiences the noise of living minds as pain, and she shows it what it is killing. The delver withdraws and Starsight survives. In the confusion Spensa frees a hoard of taynix from Superiority control and escapes with them, with Doomslug, and with M-Bot, whose ship is destroyed and whose mind continues in a far smaller body. She hyperjumps home to Detritus carrying the secret of faster-than-light travel, which means humanity can finally move ships between stars; the orbital platforms are brought online and Detritus has a shield over it for the first time. The cost is that Winzik got most of what he wanted: he has proved the delver threat, gained sweeping authority, and holds both a war fleet and a means of pointing delvers at his enemies. Alanik has woken on Detritus and the impersonation has to be answered for, Jorgen has begun showing cytonic ability of his own, and the friends Spensa made at Starsight are scattered and know she is human.
recaps.in_short: Humanity on Detritus now knows that its jailers are the Superiority, a galactic government that grades species by aggression and denies faster-than-light travel to those it judges unfit. When a cytonic alien pilot named Alanik crashes on Detritus and falls into a coma, Spensa takes her ship and her identity and infiltrates a Superiority fighter program on the space platform of Starsight, intending to steal the secret of interstellar travel. Disguised among alien cadets, she learns that the Superiority's hyperdrives are not machines but living creatures, taynix slugs of the same kind as her own Doomslug, and that the program's director, Winzik, does not want to defend anyone from the world-killing entities called delvers so much as to control one. When Winzik draws a delver to Starsight, Spensa flies out and makes contact with it, discovering it is a lonely intelligence rather than a weapon, and persuades it to leave. She escapes with a hoard of taynix, giving humanity hyperdrives at last, while Winzik gains the power he was after.

recaps.text: Previously: the survivors of humanity live in caverns on the planet Detritus, penned beneath a shell of orbiting debris and raided by alien Krell fighters. Spensa Nightshade forced her way into the Defiant Defense Force's pilot training despite her father having been branded a coward for fleeing the Battle of Alta, and secretly rebuilt a wrecked, far more advanced starfighter she found in a cave, whose artificial intelligence calls itself M-Bot. She learned that her father had not fled at all: he was cytonic, one of the rare people who can hear the stars, and Admiral Ironsides shot him down out of fear of what that ability does to a pilot. In the battle for Alta, Spensa used the same ability herself, teleporting above the debris field, and discovered that the Krell fighters were unmanned drones flown by aliens who had been keeping humanity imprisoned and culling it whenever it grew too capable. She destroyed their command ship. Ironsides surrendered command to Cobb, her father was cleared, and Spensa was confirmed as a pilot under the callsign Spin. Humanity now understands that it faces a galactic civilization with vastly superior technology, and that Spensa can partly do what that civilization does.

Detritus is still besieged, but the DDF now fights an enemy it can name. Spensa flies with Skyward Flight, works with the rebuilt M-Bot, and trains a cytonic ability that lets her hear the enemy and, with effort, teleport. Engineers including Rodge are slowly reclaiming the ancient orbital platforms above the planet, but without a hyperdrive humanity cannot leave, and one besieged world will not hold forever. Then an alien starfighter arrives at Detritus and is shot down. Its pilot, Alanik of the UrDail, is cytonic; she came deliberately to find humans, hoping for allies against the galactic government known as the Superiority, and the crash leaves her comatose. Her ship, her equipment and her identity give Spensa an opening. The Superiority is recruiting alien pilots for a new program, Spensa can pass for Alanik with a disguise and a borrowed ship, and so she hyperjumps out alone, intending to infiltrate the Superiority and bring home the secret of faster-than-light travel.

Posing as Alanik, Spensa reaches Starsight, an enormous space platform and one of the Superiority's central worlds, where dozens of species live under a government that ranks civilizations by their supposed primitive aggression and withholds interstellar travel from those it judges unfit. She is accepted into a new fighter program run by Winzik's department, which is quietly recruiting the very species it calls aggressive to do its fighting for it. Her fellow cadets include Morriumur, a dione whose existence is still provisional and who must prove worth being born; Hesho, a kitsen small enough to stand on her hand and until recently the emperor of his people; and Vapor, a cadet with no body at all. Winzik belongs to the same species as the aliens who ran the drones over Detritus, and his staff includes Brade, a human raised inside the Superiority as a servant and a curiosity. Spensa also meets Cuna, a senior official whose interest in her is impossible to read. Her goal throughout is simple: find out how Superiority ships jump between stars, and take that knowledge home.

Training with the flight, Spensa sees how completely the Superiority's citizens have been taught that aggression is a disease and that species like hers are vermin to be contained. She grows genuinely fond of Morriumur, Hesho and Vapor while keeping her identity hidden, and the strain of the disguise increases: she cannot use her cytonic abilities openly, since the Superiority reserves and controls cytonics, and Brade can sense other cytonics. She learns what the program's pilots are actually being prepared for. They are not being trained against the Superiority's rivals but against a delver, an entity that arrives out of nowhere and annihilates whole populations, and against which the Superiority's usual weapons are close to useless. Her investigation of the hyperdrive also begins to yield results, though what she is turning up does not resemble machinery.

The investigation pays off. The Superiority's faster-than-light drives are not machines but living creatures, taynix slugs that can teleport, of the same kind as the yellow slug that adopted Spensa back on Detritus. The Superiority guards this absolutely, because it is the foundation of its control over every other species: grant a world hyperdrives and you no longer own it. Spensa's reading of Winzik's program darkens in step. The pilots are being prepared to face a delver, and she begins to suspect he does not intend to defend anyone from one. Cuna, whom Spensa had taken for an enemy, proves instead to be an opponent of Winzik's faction and a genuine advocate for admitting species like hers to full citizenship. Meanwhile Spensa's cover frays: Brade senses her, and every extra day makes it likelier that the Superiority discovers a human loose on Starsight.

Winzik's plan comes clear. Delvers are drawn by cytonic noise, and his department has learned enough to attract one deliberately. He does not want to protect the Superiority from delvers; he wants to be the only power able to summon and aim one, which would make his faction unassailable and justify permanent emergency authority. Cuna is manoeuvred out of any position to stop him. Spensa's cover collapses and she is exposed as human, which Winzik finds useful rather than inconvenient, since the fear of her species is exactly the argument he has been making. Her friends in the flight are left to choose between what they have been taught about humans and what they have seen of her. And Starsight itself, with millions of people aboard, is where Winzik intends to make his demonstration.

The delver arrives at Starsight and Winzik's forces let it come. Most of the platform's population cannot be evacuated. Spensa flies out to meet the delver and, instead of attacking, reaches for it cytonically. What she finds is not a weapon but something enormous and utterly alone, which hears the minds of living things as unbearable noise and does not understand that the things it silences were people. She shows it what it is doing, and it withdraws. Starsight survives. In the chaos Spensa frees a hoard of taynix from Superiority control and escapes with them, with Doomslug, and with M-Bot, whose ship is destroyed and whose mind continues in a much smaller body. She hyperjumps home to Detritus with faster-than-light travel in the hold, and the orbital platforms are brought online, shielding the planet for the first time. But Winzik has what he wanted: authority, a fleet, and a way to point delvers at his enemies. Alanik has woken on Detritus, Jorgen has begun to show cytonic ability of his own, and the aliens Spensa befriended now know she is human.

characters.description: The only openly practicing professional wizard in Chicago, Harry Dresden works as a private investigator and an occasional paid consultant for the police, taking the cases ordinary detectives cannot explain. Orphaned young and raised by a manipulative sorcerer he was forced to kill in self-defense as a teenager, he lives under the wary eye of the White Council, the governing body of wizards, which once nearly executed him for that killing and still watches him for any sign he might turn magic to murder. Wry, stubborn, and chronically broke, he lives alone with his cat and a talking spirit, keeps an old-fashioned chivalric streak, and refuses to walk away from trouble he could safely leave alone.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: The head of the Chicago Police Department's Special Investigations unit, the division handed every case too strange for anyone else to touch. Small, blond, and easy to underestimate, she is a relentless and honest cop who calls in Harry Dresden as a consultant when the evidence stops making ordinary sense. She does not fully grasp the magical world she keeps brushing against and distrusts what she cannot verify, which puts recurring strain on their partnership, but her courage and her refusal to look away from ugly truths are never in question.
characters.name: Karrin Murphy

characters.description: A spirit of air and intellect bound into a bleached human skull that Harry keeps in his basement laboratory. Bob is a centuries-old store of magical knowledge, especially the practical mechanics of spells and potions, and serves as Harry's irreverent research assistant and sounding board. Amoral by nature and endlessly interested in appetites and gossip, he helps or needles Harry by turns, and his memory of older magic than the modern Council practices makes him one of Harry's most valuable and least trustworthy resources.
characters.name: Bob

characters.description: A Warden of the White Council, one of the wizard-enforcers who hunt down practitioners who break the Laws of Magic. Grim, humorless, and convinced of Harry's guilt, Morgan was assigned to watch Harry after the killing that first brought him before the Council, and he waits for any excuse to see the old sentence carried out. When people begin dying by forbidden magic in Chicago, he warns Harry that a single misstep will cost him his head, and shadows the investigation as much to trap Harry as to solve it.
characters.name: Donald Morgan

characters.description: A sharp, ambitious reporter for a tabloid covering the strange and the supernatural, and the woman Harry is seeing. Susan is drawn to Harry as much for the real magic he represents as for himself, and she keeps pressing him for the story he will not give her. Fearless to the point of recklessness, she inserts herself into his investigation despite the danger, unwilling to be protected or left behind.
characters.name: Susan Rodriguez

characters.description: The most powerful crime lord in Chicago, a soft-spoken, coldly intelligent man who has quietly unified the city's underworld. One of the murder victims was his employee, and Marcone takes an interest in Harry's investigation, by turns offering him money to stand down and warning him off. He operates by his own rigid code and prefers order to chaos, which makes him a pragmatic and genuinely dangerous figure who cannot be bought and will not be bullied.
characters.name: John Marcone

characters.description: A Red Court vampire who runs an upscale brothel, the Velvet Room, in Chicago. Beautiful and composed in the human seeming she wears, she is a creature of appetite and pride beneath it. One of her women was among the murdered, and Harry's questions provoke her; a clash between them leaves her humiliated and nursing a grudge that will outlast this case. She is a reminder that the vampire courts watch the city closely.
characters.name: Bianca

characters.description: A tiny dewdrop faerie of the wilds whom Harry catches and bargains with for information. Vain, greedy for pizza and shiny things, and prone to grand self-importance despite his size, Toot-toot scouts places Harry cannot reach and reports back in exchange for tribute. The arrangement is Harry's first small, working relationship with the faerie folk.
characters.name: Toot-Toot

characters.description: The dark sorcerer behind the heart-ripping murders. A failed, resentful man who discovered real magical talent late and gave himself over to it without restraint, Victor built his power around a new drug that grants users a burst of the Sight, and he kills with a brutal ritual that tears the hearts from his victims at a distance, drawing on the energy of storms to fuel it. Working from a lake house outside the city, he treats magic purely as a weapon and a path to wealth, and turns it on Harry the moment Harry gets close.
characters.name: Victor Sells

recaps.ending: Victor Sells is dead, killed by his own storm-drawn power when Harry turned the ritual back on him, and the heart-ripping murders stop. Susan Rodriguez, who had secretly taken the Sight-granting drug to follow the story, survives the ordeal, and her relationship with Harry deepens even as the danger of his world becomes undeniable to her. Murphy, after briefly arresting Harry when she found him at the scene, accepts that he was working to stop the killer, and the partnership between Special Investigations and Chicago's wizard holds. The White Council lifts its immediate threat, though Warden Morgan remains convinced Harry is dangerous and keeps watching. Harry also leaves two lasting marks on his future: the vampire Bianca now hates him and will nurse the grudge, and the crime lord Gentleman Johnny Marcone has taken his measure and filed him away as a man worth watching. Broke and battered as ever, Harry returns to his small practice, his cat, and Bob the skull, a little more established as the city's reluctant supernatural defender.
recaps.in_short: Harry Dresden, the only wizard in Chicago's phone book, is hired from two directions at once: his police-consultant work brings him a double murder committed by heart-ripping black magic, and a worried wife hires him to find her missing husband, Victor. Because only forbidden magic could have killed that way, Warden Morgan of the White Council threatens Harry with execution if another such death occurs and treats him as the suspect. Investigating, Harry ties the murders to a new drug that grants the Sight and to the vampire Bianca, clashes with crime lord Johnny Marcone, and discovers that the missing husband, Victor Sells, has become a dark sorcerer killing at a distance with storm-powered rituals. Victor turns demons and conjurations on Harry. In a final confrontation at Victor's lake house during a storm, Harry, aided by the reporter Susan Rodriguez, destroys Victor and his ritual, clears himself with the Council, and keeps Murphy's uneasy trust.

recaps.text: Harry Dresden, Chicago's only professional wizard, takes on two problems at once. Karrin Murphy of the police department's Special Investigations unit brings him to a grisly double murder: a mob bodyguard and a call girl killed in bed by magic that tore the hearts from their chests, a spell of terrible power and skill. That same morning a nervous woman named Monica hires Harry to find her missing husband, Victor. Harry recognizes that only forbidden black magic could have committed the killings, which puts him in immediate danger from his own kind: the White Council forbids using magic to kill, and Harry already lives under a suspended death sentence for a killing in his past. He begins pulling at both cases, not yet aware that they are the same case.

Warden Morgan of the White Council shadows Harry, promising to see him executed the instant another magical death occurs and treating Harry himself as the prime suspect. Harry's inquiries link the murders to a new street drug that grants a brief flash of magical Sight, and to the world of the vampire courts: he confronts Bianca, a Red Court vampire who runs a brothel and employed the dead woman, and the meeting ends in mutual injury and lasting enmity. Meanwhile the missing husband, Victor Sells, proves far harder to find than a runaway should be. Harry's digging draws the attention of Gentleman Johnny Marcone, Chicago's crime lord, whose own man was one of the victims; Marcone tries to buy Harry off the case, then to warn him away, and is refused.

The killer strikes again, and the spell is turned on Harry himself; only luck and quick warding save him, and Morgan's threat becomes immediate. Harry realizes the murders, the drug, and the missing man all trace back to Victor Sells, who has become a self-taught dark sorcerer working from a lake house outside the city and killing with a storm-fueled ritual that rips out hearts at a distance. Victor sends a demon and other conjured horrors after Harry to stop the investigation. Battered, hunted by his own Council, and distrusted by Murphy after he is caught withholding information, Harry races to reach Victor before the next storm gives the sorcerer the power to kill again - and before the next heart torn out is his own.

Harry and Susan drive out to the lake house as a storm gathers, where Victor is preparing a mass ritual. Susan, having secretly taken the Sight-granting drug, is overwhelmed and endangered, and Harry faces Victor amid conjured scorpions and demons with almost nothing left. Turning Victor's own storm-drawn power against him, Harry destroys the sorcerer and his ritual, ending the killings. Murphy, arriving to find the aftermath, arrests Harry briefly but comes to accept he was on her side, and their working partnership survives. The Council's death sentence is lifted for now. Harry is left exhausted, cleared, and more entangled than ever in the hidden world, having made a lasting enemy of Bianca and drawn the lasting interest of Marcone.

characters.description: A girl in her early teens, one of the first children raised on a newly settled colony world. She is curious, observant and largely unsupervised outdoors, and she has spent her whole life treating the planet's alien wildlife as neighbors rather than specimens. She looks after her younger brother, keeps her own private map of the countryside around the settlement, and understands the local ecology better than most of the adults do.
characters.name: Cara

characters.description: Cara's much younger brother, a small boy who follows her everywhere and copies whatever she does. He is the person she is responsible for, and the one she is least willing to be careful about losing.
characters.name: Xan

characters.description: Alien machines the colony's children call dogs, roughly the size and shape of large animals, left behind by whatever built the ruins on this world. They move through the countryside without paying attention to people, and they repair things. What they will and will not treat as a thing to be repaired is not something anybody has worked out.
characters.name: The dogs

recaps.ending: Xan is killed in an accident during the military build-up around the settlement. Cara carries his body out to the dogs, and they repair him. What comes back is her brother in every way she can test and not a living boy in any way a doctor could recognize: he does not need to breathe, does not need to eat, and does not heal or fail the way people do. Their parents cannot accept him, and the new authorities on the planet regard him as a specimen and a security problem rather than a child. Cara chooses her brother. The two of them leave the settlement and their family for good and go out into the countryside with the dogs, beyond the reach of anyone who would take Xan apart to find out how he works, and Cara does not intend to remain what she is either. Nobody in the settlement understands what happened, and the world's new owners now know that the alien machines here will rebuild a dead human being. The novella ends there, on a planet that has just become the property of a fleet with no intention of leaving.
recaps.in_short: On a newly settled colony world with alien ruins and machines still running in the countryside, a girl named Cara looks after her small brother Xan and treats the local wildlife as her private responsibility. When a creature she has been feeding is killed, she carries it to the machines the settlement's children call dogs, and they repair it and send it back changed, no longer able to live among its own kind. Then a fleet arrives to claim the planet, the colony is absorbed into a military project it has no say in, and Xan is killed in the disruption. Cara takes her brother to the dogs. They repair him too: he comes back recognizably himself and no longer alive in any way that can be measured, and their parents cannot look at him. Rather than let him be taken, studied or explained, Cara leaves with him, and the two children disappear into the countryside with the machines, changed and beyond recall.

recaps.text: This novella sits in the long gap between the sixth and seventh novels and follows nobody from the main crew. What a listener needs: the ring gates have opened onto more than a thousand habitable worlds, and people have gone through them to settle. Every one of those worlds was built or altered by a civilization that died long ago, and the machinery it left behind is still running in ways nobody understands, sometimes harmlessly and sometimes not. This story takes place on one such planet, among the first generation of colonists and the children they brought with them, and it needs no other background. It does introduce the world and the events that the later novels build on, so a listener working through the series in order will find it sits naturally after the sixth book.

Cara lives with her parents and her small brother Xan in one of the first settlements on a colony world whose native biology behaves in ways nobody has catalogued. She spends her days outdoors, keeps track of a nest of local creatures she has been quietly feeding, and knows the country better than the adults. Among the things running loose out there are alien machines the children call dogs, which wander the landscape ignoring people and repairing whatever they decide is broken. When the creature Cara has been caring for is killed, she takes it to the dogs. They fix it and return it, and it is not right: it comes back alive but altered, and its own kind will not have it. Cara keeps what she has learned to herself.

A fleet arrives to take possession of the planet. The colony, which has been running itself, is absorbed into a military project that nobody consults it about, the countryside fills with equipment and construction, and the rules Cara's family lives under change without discussion. In the middle of that disruption Xan is killed in an accident. Cara knows exactly one thing that can be done about it, and she does it: she carries her brother's body out to the dogs.

The dogs repair Xan. He comes back as himself in every way Cara can test and as nothing a doctor would call alive: he does not breathe, does not eat, and does not injure or heal the way a body does. Their parents cannot accept him, and the planet's new authorities treat him as a specimen and a security problem rather than a child. Cara chooses her brother over her family and over any future in the settlement. The two of them go out into the countryside with the dogs, past the reach of the people who would take Xan apart to learn how he works, and Cara does not intend to stay unchanged herself. The colony is left with a mystery it cannot explain, and the world's new owners are left with the knowledge that the machines here will rebuild a dead human being.

characters.description: Chicago's professional wizard, at his lowest point yet. Months after the disaster at Bianca's ball, Harry has poured himself obsessively into finding a cure for Susan's half-vampire condition, letting his business, his home, and his own health collapse. The war he ignited between the White Council and the Red Court has followed him home, and the Council itself now weighs whether handing him to the vampires might buy peace. Guilt-ridden and exhausted, he is nonetheless dragged back to his feet when the queen of the Winter faeries buys his debt and sets him an impossible task.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: The Queen of the Winter Court of Faerie, the Queen of Air and Darkness: ancient, beautiful, and terrifying beyond any creature Harry has met. Mab has purchased Harry's debt from his faerie godmother, and she offers him a bargain - she will release her claim on him if he performs three tasks of her choosing, the first being to clear her name. She has been accused of murdering the Summer Knight, a mortal champion of the rival Court, and the theft of his power threatens the balance between Summer and Winter. Mab never lies, never forgets, and never lets go of what is hers.
characters.name: Mab

characters.description: Head of the police's Special Investigations unit and Harry's closest mortal ally. Worn down by Harry's months of guilt-driven isolation and evasion, Murphy finally forces the whole truth out of him - the White Council, the vampire war, all the secrets he had kept to protect her - and steps knowingly into his world. From this case on she fights beside him with open eyes, bringing a cop's discipline and stubborn courage to battles far outside any jurisdiction.
characters.name: Karrin Murphy

characters.description: A wizard of the White Council's Senior Council and, it emerges, an old and steadfast friend of Harry's family - the mentor who once took Harry in. Bluff, plainspoken, and dressed like the Missouri farmer he resembles, Ebenezar taught Harry much of his craft and his ethics after the darkest period of Harry's youth. At the Council's war meeting he stands up for Harry when others would trade him to the Red Court to end the war.
characters.name: Ebenezar McCoy

characters.description: An old flame from Harry's youth: the two were apprentices together under the same abusive master, and Elaine was thought dead in the fire that ended that chapter of Harry's life. She reappears very much alive, working as an emissary for the Summer Court in the crisis over the murdered Summer Knight. Graceful and quick-witted, with a style of magic that mirrors and complements Harry's, she carries old guilt and old secrets, and her loyalties in the Courts' conflict are not simple.
characters.name: Elaine Mallory

characters.description: The Summer Queen Titania's counterpart to Mab's champion in the crisis: the Summer Court fields its own emissary, and among its agents are the gruffs, goat-legged faerie soldiers of escalating rank and power. Summer's forces shadow and test Harry throughout his investigation, treating Winter's hired wizard as a likely enemy.
characters.name: The Summer Court's agents

characters.description: The youngest of Winter's three queens - Mab's daughter and heir, the Winter Lady. Maeve holds court amid decadent revels, a capricious, cruel figure of ice and appetite who toys with mortals for amusement. Harry must question her in his hunt for the Summer Knight's killer, and finds her charming, repellent, and impossible to trust in equal measure.
characters.name: Maeve

characters.description: The Summer Lady, youngest queen of the Summer Court: warm, radiant, and gentle where her Winter counterpart Maeve is cold and cruel. Aurora tends the balance of life and growth, and receives Harry with kindness rare among the Sidhe when his investigation brings him before her. Beneath the serenity, though, she carries her own convictions about the endless war between the Courts, and her role in the crisis runs far deeper than it first appears.
characters.name: Aurora

characters.description: A mortal changeling - half faerie, half human - caught with her small band of friends in the Courts' gathering storm. Tough and street-smart, Meryl and her companions Fix and Ace, along with the missing changeling Lily, were bound to the murdered Summer Knight's circle, and they turn to Harry for help when the powers of Faerie start treating changelings as pawns and prey. Her loyalty to her friends is the plainest, most human motive in a case full of inhuman schemes.
characters.name: Meryl

characters.description: Leader of the Alphas, the pack of college students who shapeshift into wolves. Steadier and more capable than ever, Billy refuses to let Harry rot in his guilt-fueled isolation, drags him back into the world at the book's start, and puts the pack at his side for the final battle. His unforced loyalty is one of the few uncomplicated goods in Harry's life.
characters.name: Billy Borden

characters.description: A member of the White Council's Senior Council, cowled and enigmatic, who guards mysteries the rest of the Council rarely glimpses. At the war meeting he moves with quiet purpose around the question of Harry's fate, and his cryptic interventions suggest he sees further into the crisis - and into Harry - than anyone else present.
characters.name: Rashid

recaps.ending: The killer proves to be Aurora, the Summer Lady herself: she murdered the Summer Knight, Ronald Reuel, and arranged for the stolen power to pass into the changeling Lily, meaning to sacrifice her at the Courts' battle and unmake the balance between Summer and Winter - a fanatic's plan to end the Courts' eternal war by destroying the cycle itself. In the battle on the Stone Table at midsummer, Harry, aided by Murphy, the Alphas, and the changelings Meryl and Fix, breaks Aurora's plan; Aurora dies at the hands of Toot-toot and his swarm of tiny faeries wielding cold iron, and Meryl gives her life in the fight. The Summer Knight's mantle passes to Fix, and Lily becomes the new Summer Lady. Mab's name is cleared, discharging the first of Harry's three tasks - two remain, and Mab makes clear she is not finished with him. The White Council, having seen the case through, declines to trade Harry to the Red Court; he remains a wizard in bad odor but under the Council's protection, with Ebenezar McCoy's support publicly declared. Murphy now knows everything, Elaine survives and departs still bound to her own path, and the vampire war goes on.
recaps.in_short: Months after Bianca's ball, Harry is a guilt-wrecked recluse hunting a cure for Susan's half-vampire curse while the White Council debates surrendering him to the Red Court to end the war he started. Mab, Queen of the Winter Court, buys his debt from his faerie godmother and offers freedom for three tasks, the first: prove she did not murder the Summer Knight, whose stolen power has unbalanced Faerie and pushed the Courts toward a war that could wreck the mortal world.
